sections.html: Synodontis batensoda reaches a length of about 25 cm and should be kept in larger aquaria. It comes from Nigeria.
S. batensoda attains a length of about 25 cm and should be kept in larger aquaria.

Quite a number of Synodontis species tend to swim upside down. The best known is the upside-down cat, Synodontis nigriventris from the Congo. Synodontis batensoda shows a similar behaviour.

It seems to be quite unimportant for the fish which position it actually swims in. However, the very dark coloration of the belly shows that the upside-down position is used very often. Fish species with a "normal" swimming behaviour have light bellies, so they do not contrast much with the sky. Many predatory fish hunt from below, so this coloration is necessary.

The species is quite social and should never be kept alone. S. batensoda will eat small fish, but is usually very peaceful towards other, larger species.
Formerly S. batensoda was placed in the monotypic genus Brachysynodontis.
